source.title: 7. Diabetes Technology: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes. 7. Diabetes technology: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl. 1):S150–S165.

guideline_boundary: Recommendations are represented as panel/guideline statements using author_conclusion plus guideline_recommendation tags. Quantitative effects reported from underlying studies are tagged secondary_reported_result and remain anchored to this chapter.
schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated guideline_recommendation atom kind, so formal recommendations use author_conclusion plus descriptive tags.
Recommendation evidence grades are stored in tags because the current schema has no dedicated evidence-grade field.
Secondary narrative evidence that lacks enough structured quantitative context is not forced into quantitative_result objects.
extraction_limitations: The full ADA guideline-development methodology and evidence-grade definitions are in the separate Introduction and Methodology, which was not supplied with this section.
Bibliography entries were not atomized; they are preserved in the reference task queue.
All atoms remain needs_review because this run does not represent an independent human verification step.
No external current-practice or regulatory verification was performed because @VERIFY was not activated.
protocol_version_note: The project names summary-evaluation-appraisal-protocol-v4-compact.md as governing. Its internal heading says Integrated Compact v3. The v4-named project file was followed as authoritative and the naming mismatch was not silently repaired.
